items.title: 69537_Jimmy Jones oral history interview
items.q: I used to listen to the Glenn Miller Orchestra... and I liked Glenn Miller's work

ctx.x: And then looking at the Empire State Building. Boy, that was like Alice in Wonderland. And the enthusiasm of youth at that time, you know? Because I used to listen to the Glenn Miller Orchestra, the Army orchestra he had before he went overseas, you know, and I liked Glenn Miller's work, and I was allowed to go into the NBC Radio Center, you know, and look at the scores and everything. You know, I was just -- they just let me in. And I was so surprised to see -- that's one thing about New York, you would see the…

cities. And I'd run into guys like Paul Whiteman in the elevator, and you know, people that you just knew of. And they talked with you, you know, and said, 'Wait, look, I'm going across the street and have a beer and a corned beef sandwich. Want to join me?' And I'm sitting there looking ga-ga, you know?
